attacker_service_has_many_slots.meaning: attacker created a service with many slots for the purpose of the attack
attacker_service_has_many_slots.checkpoint: before registration of victim address as instance

service_in_active_registration.meaning: service is kept at ActiveRegistration state to register instances without intent to deploy
service_in_active_registration.checkpoint: before registration of victim address as instance

victim_is_operator_address.meaning: the victim's address is an operator address used to register agent instances
victim_is_operator_address.checkpoint: before registration of victim address as instance

operator_registered_instance_count.meaning: number of registered agent instances mapped to the operator address
operator_registered_instance_count.checkpoint: while operator address is in use as operator

operator_address_used_as_instance.meaning: the operator address is used as an agent instance address while still in use as an operator address

operator_permanently_blocked_from_regist.meaning: the other operator is permanently blocked from registering any agent instance for any service in the future (DoS)
operator_permanently_blocked_from_regist.checkpoint: after attacker registration of victim address as instance

assumptions: The operator address is in use as an operator address (registered instance count tracked in ServiceManager).

unresolved.description: The report does not give a concrete numeric definition of the operator registered instance count mapping; it is described only qualitatively in the remediation.

limitations: The permanent-block impact is encoded as a grounded Boolean because the report provides no more specific observable for the DoS outcome.
The operator registered instance count is bound to a cross-contract ServiceManager mapping that does not yet exist in the vulnerable code; binding risk is high.
